evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` computed check (lines 1104-1116) verifies only that both manager PIDs are positive and differ and that both invocation_ids are present and differ. A guest reboot occurring between the `before` and `after` manager snapshots changes the manager PID and invocation id, so this pair would pass even though the observations span a reboot, producing a false 'isolated manager restart' proof. Elsewhere the script already exposes per-snapshot `boot_id` (e.g. lines 1117-1124 read `(reboot.get("before") or {}).get("boot_id")`), and the manager snapshots share the same inspect-snapshot shape, so requiring nonempty equal boot IDs in the manager pair is the smallest compatible fail-closed fix; it complements the PID/invocation-id checks so an unchanged manager on one boot still cannot pass. This is an ordinary correctness repair to an existing intended check, not an accepted limitation (the current contract is silent on vm-feasibility and sets no contrary rule) and not a scope/approval expansion, so no owner decision is needed.
